html:
Manuel I Komnenos was Byzantine emperor from 1143 to 1180, the last of the three great emperors of the Komnenian restoration. The son of John II, he wanted to make the empire again the great power of the Mediterranean.

He fought on many fronts:

  • He handled the Second Crusade as it passed through his lands in 1147.
  • He invaded Norman southern Italy in the 1150s, without lasting success.
  • He made Hungary and Serbia client states and won land on the Danube and the Adriatic.
  • He made the crusader principality of Antioch accept him as overlord, and planned a joint invasion of Egypt with the kingdom of Jerusalem.

Manuel admired Western knights, held tournaments, married two Latin princesses, and gave posts and trade privileges to Italians, which made many Greeks resentful. In 1171 he turned on the Venetians in the mass arrests of that year. In 1176 the Seljuk sultan of Rum beat him at Myriokephalon, ending hopes of retaking central Anatolia. After his death his young son's regency collapsed into the reign of Andronikos I.
